findings: Resolved and used the fixed local PDF. Its 43-page count and SHA-256 match the previous audit and source register. The cover identifies Bernhard Stankewitz and arXiv:2210.07850v1, stamped 14 October 2022. Equivalence with the journal text is not asserted.

Freshly extracted all main-document pages 1-24 and enumerated the actual bold Theorem headings: 1.2 on page 5, 1.8 on page 9 and 5.1 on page 23. All three statements fit on their recorded pages. The references finish on page 24; a page-25 heading-only crop verifies Appendix A. No appendix body was read.

Visually compared the three full stored statements with the registered PDF. Theorem 1.2 retains its chained inequality, minimum over all nonnegative iterations, classical oracle, overbarred noise proxy, penalty lower bound and absolute empirical-noise estimation error. The second inequality does not replace the first.

Theorem 1.8 retains all four named assumptions, a two-sided absolute error bound for the empirical noise estimate, c>0 and the population-risk conclusion. Theorem 5.1 instead has only an upper error bound, c>=0, a sufficiently large positive AIC coefficient, the lower bound on tau_two-step itself and a risk conclusion on the corresponding event.

Checked all 17 source entries against the defining passages on pages 1-6, 8, 15, 21 and 22. The sampling/rank conditions, model sequence, geometric empirical projector and every line of Algorithm 1 are preserved. The algorithm uses raw-column normalization, without an invented residualized-column selection rule.

The residual fragment from (1.2) is distinct from the updated estimated-noise stopping rule (1.8). The latter uses an input estimator of empirical noise energy, not a mandatory Scaled Lasso estimator or the population variance. The classical oracle m^o is distinct from the proof-only balanced oracle.

Both (Sparse) alternatives remain intact: support size, little-o growth, signal norm and beta-min in the first branch; bounded coefficient ell2 norm and the uniform subset inequality in the gamma branch. Empty-support and gamma=1 endpoint conventions remain unresolved rather than excluded.

The design MGF condition retains all unit directions and unit coordinate variances, without requiring independent coordinates. The covariance assumption retains its lower eigenvalue bound, strict subset-coefficient bound and cutoff M_n involving both noise and design proxies. The later weak-bound restatement is archived separately.

The population geometric projector and bias are distinct from the empirical fitted-value projector. The malformed printed B_m assignment and dimensionally inconsistent empirical matrix formula remain unchanged in original passages, with explanatory notes separate from quotations.

Rate (1.20) and iteration (3.2) preserve the same selected sparsity branch. The exact-sparse threshold is first support coverage; the gamma-sparse threshold is first population-bias crossing. The value of that iteration uses the OMP path, not a noise estimator merely mentioned in its introductory context.

The additive AIC definition spans pages 21-22, and the two-step rule minimizes it over the computed prefix through tau. The source multiplicative HDAIC in the later remark is not substituted. Ties, infinite stopping times and estimator-range conventions remain as recorded source limitations.

Checked all twelve ambient passages against pages 3-5, 7, 9 and 10, including normalized empirical inner products, population norms, vector/function overloading, constants independent of n and the noise/design proxies, and the simultaneous high-probability event convention.

Reviewed 30 direct dependencies and the recursive source graph. Theorem 1.2 has no sparsity, subgaussian-design, covariance-bound, target-rate or population-projector dependency. Theorem 1.8 uses a population norm without needing a projector. Theorem 5.1 reaches the population projector through (3.2). The graph has 37 deduplicated related-theorem connections.

Checked all source keywords, naming contexts and highlight selectors against their source passages and related theorems. Assumptions remain labeled as assumptions, model prose as a source passage, and unnumbered conditions as conditions. Empirical and population projections retain separate source records despite sharing an original term.

All six census-content JSON files passed manual review unchanged. Archived the existing scripts and retained a per-paper rebuild entry point that resolves the registered PDF and writes only to an empty output directory. All six artifacts reproduced byte for byte. Independent validation checks structure and consistency; it does not substitute for manual source review or certify proofs.
